review: skipped 601.3f: the reason named Gonti as the only such card; Praetor's Grasp grants look-and-play too, reason reworded to cover every such card.
601.2f-2: Painter's Servant asks for a color choice as it enters, which no decision fixed; swapped it for the vanilla {2} artifact creature Bronze Sable.

601.3e-1: the decisions cast Giant Killer and then tried Chop Down from the same library card, which the first cast would have moved; rewrote them as one playability evaluation of both halves from the same state.

601.8-1: the scenario cast Shock while Sphere of Resistance was still on the stack, which shows only that a static ability does nothing on the stack; rebuilt it so Shock is already on the stack when Sphere is cast and resolves (Shock unaffected), against the order where Sphere resolves first (Shock unaffordable with three Mountains).

skipped.reason: cannot be illustrated in Forge: every card that lets a player cast a face-down exiled card (Gonti, Lord of Luxury; Praetor's Grasp) grants the permission to look at it together with the permission to cast it, so no state exists in which a player may cast the card but cannot look at it

scenarios.title: Casting moves the spell from the hand to the stack and pays its cost; a cast that cannot be completed is not made
decisions: A casts Lightning Bolt targeting B, tapping Mountain for {R}.
A passes priority, then B passes priority; Lightning Bolt resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Lightning Bolt moves from A's hand to the stack as the topmost object with A as its controller and Mountain becomes tapped; when it resolves B's life is 17 and Lightning Bolt is in A's graveyard.

variants.label: no-mana
variants.delta: A's only Mountain starts tapped.
variants.expected: The cast is not made: A cannot pay {R}, Lightning Bolt stays in A's hand, the stack is empty, and B's life is 20.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge never offers an unpayable spell, so the second variant is shown as can_play = false on the playability record rather than as a reverted attempt.

scenarios.title: A continuous effect that modifies a spell's characteristics applies as the spell is put on the stack

setup.notes: Painter's Servant entered earlier and its controller chose blue.

decisions: A casts Shock targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Mountain; A passes priority.
B casts Pyroblast choosing the mode 'counter target spell if it's blue', targeting Shock, tapping Mountain; B passes priority, then A passes priority; Pyroblast resolves.
After Pyroblast resolves, both players pass priority again.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Shock is red and blue as it sits on the stack, so Pyroblast counters it: Shock moves to A's graveyard without resolving, Grizzly Bears has no damage and stays on the battlefield, and Pyroblast is in B's graveyard.

variants.label: green
variants.delta: Painter's Servant's controller chose green instead of blue.
variants.expected: Shock is red and green, so Pyroblast resolves and does nothing (it is not a fizzle: its target is still legal); Pyroblast is in B's graveyard, then Shock resolves: Grizzly Bears is dealt 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge's Painter's Servant uses AffectedZone$ All, which should cover the stack.

scenarios.title: One instance of the word 'target' cannot choose the same object twice

setup.notes: Undo is a sorcery with {1}{U}{U}; it needs two target creatures.

decisions: A attempts to cast Undo with Grizzly Bears as both of its two targets, tapping three Islands.

variants.label: one-creature
variants.expected: Illegal: Grizzly Bears cannot be chosen twice, no second creature exists, so Undo has no legal two-target choice (has_legal_target false, can_play false); Undo stays in A's hand and the Islands stay untapped.

variants.label: two-creatures
variants.delta: B also controls Craw Wurm; A chooses Grizzly Bears and Craw Wurm as the two targets.
variants.expected: Legal: Undo can be cast (has_legal_target true, can_play true); when it resolves Grizzly Bears and Craw Wurm return to B's hand.

scenarios.title: A spell that uses the word 'target' twice may choose the same object once for each instance

setup.notes: Dryad Arbor is both a land and a creature. Spiteful Blow is 'Destroy target creature and target land.'

decisions: A casts Spiteful Blow choosing Dryad Arbor as the target creature and Dryad Arbor as the target land, tapping six Swamps.
Both players pass priority; Spiteful Blow resolves.

variants.label: same-object
variants.expected: Legal (can_play true, Dryad Arbor is a legal choice for each instance of 'target'); on resolution Dryad Arbor is destroyed and moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: two-objects
variants.delta: B controls Forest and Grizzly Bears instead of Dryad Arbor; A chooses Grizzly Bears as the target creature and Forest as the target land.
variants.expected: Legal: when Spiteful Blow resolves Grizzly Bears and Forest are both destroyed and move to B's graveyard.

variants.label: no-creature
variants.delta: B controls only a Forest, no creature, instead of Dryad Arbor.
variants.expected: Illegal: there is no legal target creature (has_legal_target false, can_play false); Spiteful Blow stays in A's hand and the Swamps stay untapped.

scenarios.title: An effect that says a spell must target a particular permanent restricts the caster's choice of targets

setup.notes: Standard Bearer is a Flagbearer: while an opponent chooses targets for a spell, that player must choose a Flagbearer if able.

decisions: A attempts to cast Shock choosing Grizzly Bears as its target.

variants.label: other-target
variants.expected: Illegal: A must choose Standard Bearer if able, so Grizzly Bears is not an allowed target (the legal targets are only Standard Bearer); Shock stays in A's hand and Mountain stays untapped.

variants.label: flagbearer
variants.delta: A chooses Standard Bearer as Shock's target.
variants.expected: Legal: Shock is cast, Mountain is tapped; when it resolves Standard Bearer is dealt 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: no-flagbearer
variants.delta: Standard Bearer is not on B's battlefield (B controls only Grizzly Bears); A chooses Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Legal: no must-target effect applies; Shock is cast and, when it resolves, Grizzly Bears moves to B's graveyard.

scenarios.title: A proposed spell that cannot legally be cast is not cast and the game returns to the moment before
decisions: A attempts to cast Doom Blade on B's only creature, tapping two Swamps.

variants.label: black-target
variants.expected: Illegal: Child of Night is black, so Doom Blade has no legal target (has_legal_target false, can_play false); the game returns to the moment before the cast, Doom Blade is in A's hand, the Swamps are untapped, and the stack is empty.

variants.label: nonblack-target
variants.delta: B's creature is Grizzly Bears instead of Child of Night.
variants.expected: Legal: Doom Blade is cast on Grizzly Bears (can_play true, Swamps tapped); when it resolves Grizzly Bears moves to B's graveyard.

scenarios.title: A cost increase raises the total cost of a spell
decisions: A attempts to cast Shock targeting B, tapping Mountain.

variants.label: taxed
variants.expected: Shock's total cost is {1}{R}, more than A's single Mountain can pay: can_play false, Shock stays in A's hand.

variants.label: untaxed
variants.delta: Sphere of Resistance is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Shock's total cost is {R}: can_play true; A casts it by tapping Mountain and when it resolves B's life is 18.

variants.label: taxed-payable
variants.delta: A controls two Mountains (Sphere of Resistance still on B's battlefield).
variants.expected: Shock's total cost is {1}{R}: can_play true; A taps both Mountains and when it resolves B's life is 18.

scenarios.title: A cost reduction lowers the total cost but never below zero

setup.notes: Foundry Inspector: artifact spells you cast cost {1} less.

decisions: A casts Bronze Sable (cost {2}), tapping Mountain for the one generic mana left after the reduction.
Both players pass priority; Bronze Sable resolves.

variants.label: reduced
variants.expected: Bronze Sable's total cost is {1}: A taps its Mountain and no more mana is needed, and Bronze Sable enters the battlefield.

variants.label: floor
variants.delta: A casts Ornithopter (cost {0}) instead of Bronze Sable.
variants.expected: Ornithopter's total cost stays {0}: it is cast with no mana, Mountain stays untapped, and Ornithopter enters the battlefield.

variants.label: no-mana
variants.delta: A's Mountain starts tapped.
variants.expected: Bronze Sable's total cost is {1}, not {0}: it cannot be paid, can_play false, and Bronze Sable stays in A's hand.

scenarios.title: The total cost is locked in before costs are paid, so sacrificing the cost reducer does not raise it

setup.notes: Thunderscape Familiar: black spells and green spells you cast cost {1} less. Altar's Reap costs {1}{B} and has an additional cost of sacrificing a creature.

decisions: A casts Altar's Reap, sacrificing Thunderscape Familiar as the additional cost and tapping Swamp for {B}.
Both players pass priority; Altar's Reap resolves.

variants.label: familiar-sacrificed
variants.expected: The total cost {B} is locked in while Thunderscape Familiar is still on the battlefield, so one Swamp pays it even though the Familiar is sacrificed: Altar's Reap is cast, Thunderscape Familiar is in A's graveyard, and when Altar's Reap resolves A draws two cards.

variants.label: no-familiar
variants.delta: Thunderscape Familiar is not on the battlefield; A sacrifices Grizzly Bears as the additional cost.
variants.expected: The total cost is {1}{B}, which A's single Swamp cannot pay: can_play false, Altar's Reap stays in A's hand and Grizzly Bears stays on the battlefield.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge applies cost reductions when it builds the cost; check that it does not recompute it after the sacrifice choice.

scenarios.title: The total cost is paid in full, and a cost that cannot be paid stops the cast
decisions: A casts Altar's Reap, sacrificing Grizzly Bears and tapping both Swamps.
Both players pass priority; Altar's Reap resolves.

variants.label: both-costs
variants.expected: A pays the mana and the sacrifice: both Swamps are tapped, Grizzly Bears is in A's graveyard, Altar's Reap is on the stack and, when it resolves, A draws two cards.

variants.label: no-sacrifice
variants.delta: A controls no creature (Grizzly Bears is not on the battlefield).
variants.expected: The sacrifice cost cannot be paid and partial payment is not allowed: Altar's Reap is not cast, stays in A's hand, and neither Swamp is tapped.

scenarios.title: A 'whenever you cast' ability triggers once the spell has been cast, before the spell resolves
decisions: A casts Shock targeting B, tapping Mountain.
Young Pyromancer's trigger goes on the stack above Shock; both players pass priority until the stack is empty.

variants.label: instant
variants.expected: Young Pyromancer's trigger fires when Shock is cast and resolves before Shock: A controls a 1/1 red Elemental token, then Shock resolves and B's life is 18.

variants.label: creature
variants.delta: A casts Mons's Goblin Raiders (a creature spell) instead of Shock.
variants.expected: Young Pyromancer's trigger does not fire: A gets no Elemental token, and Mons's Goblin Raiders enters the battlefield.

scenarios.title: A player can begin to cast a spell only if no rule or effect prohibits it
decisions: A attempts to cast Grizzly Bears, tapping Forest and Mountain.

variants.label: prohibited
variants.expected: Steel Golem's effect prohibits it: Grizzly Bears cannot be cast (can_play false) and stays in A's hand.

variants.label: not-prohibited-spell
variants.delta: A casts Shock (not a creature spell) targeting B instead.
variants.expected: Allowed: can_play true; Shock is cast and, when it resolves, B's life is 18.

variants.label: opposing-golem
variants.delta: Steel Golem is on B's battlefield instead of A's.
variants.expected: Allowed: Steel Golem only prohibits its controller's creature spells; Grizzly Bears can be cast (can_play true) and enters the battlefield.

scenarios.title: A prohibition that a choice made during proposal could avoid does not stop the player from beginning to cast

setup.notes: Void Winnower: your opponents can't cast spells with even mana values. Rolling Thunder is a sorcery with mana cost {X}{R}{R}.

decisions: B announces X = 1 for Rolling Thunder (mana value 3), assigns its 1 damage to A, and taps three Mountains.
Both players pass priority; Rolling Thunder resolves.

variants.label: odd-x
variants.expected: B may begin casting Rolling Thunder (can_play true) although its mana value with X = 0 is even; with X = 1 its mana value is odd, so the cast is legal, three Mountains are tapped, and when it resolves A's life is 19.

variants.label: fixed-even
variants.delta: B holds Goblin Piker (mana value 2) instead of Rolling Thunder.
variants.expected: No choice can change Goblin Piker's mana value, so Void Winnower prohibits it: can_play false and Goblin Piker stays in B's hand.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge may evaluate Rolling Thunder with X = 0 when it decides playability; check it lets B begin the cast.

scenarios.title: A cast-as-though-flash permission for Auras applies when a choice made during proposal (bestow) makes the spell an Aura

setup.notes: Sigarda's Aid: you may cast Aura and Equipment spells as though they had flash. Cavern Lampad is an Enchantment Creature with bestow {5}{B}.

decisions: A, with priority in B's end step, casts Cavern Lampad for its bestow cost targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping six Swamps.

variants.label: bestow
variants.expected: Legal: the bestow cast is an Aura spell, so Sigarda's Aid gives it flash (can_play true for the bestow ability); Cavern Lampad is on the stack and, when it resolves, attaches to Grizzly Bears.

variants.label: creature-cast
variants.delta: A casts Cavern Lampad for its normal mana cost {3}{B} instead of its bestow cost.
variants.expected: Illegal: as a creature spell it has no flash (can_play false for the normal cast); Cavern Lampad stays in A's hand.

variants.label: no-aid
variants.delta: Sigarda's Aid is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Illegal: nothing gives the bestow cast flash, so it cannot be cast in B's end step (can_play false).

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge treats the bestow cast as a separate spell ability; check that Card.Aura in Sigarda's Aid matches a bestow spell rather than only the Aura card type.

scenarios.title: A cast-as-though-flash permission that requires paying more lets the player begin casting at instant speed

setup.notes: Rout ({3}{W}{W}, sorcery): you may cast it as though it had flash if you pay {2} more.

decisions: A, with priority in B's end step, casts Rout paying the extra {2}, tapping seven Plains.
Both players pass priority; Rout resolves.

variants.label: pays-more
variants.expected: Legal: total cost is {5}{W}{W} (7 mana); can_play true at instant speed; when Rout resolves Grizzly Bears is destroyed and moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: cannot-pay-more
variants.delta: A controls six Plains instead of seven.
variants.expected: The flash cast needs 7 mana and A has 6: can_play false in B's end step; Rout stays in A's hand.

variants.label: own-turn
variants.delta: It is A's turn, main phase 1 and the stack is empty (A still has seven Plains).
variants.expected: Rout is cast at sorcery speed for its normal cost {3}{W}{W}: can_play true, five Plains tapped and Grizzly Bears destroyed when it resolves.

scenarios.title: A spell that has flash only when a condition holds can be begun at instant speed when it holds

setup.notes: Illusion Spinners: you may cast this spell as though it had flash if you control a Faerie.

decisions: A, with priority in B's end step, casts Illusion Spinners, tapping five Islands.

variants.label: faerie
variants.expected: Legal: A controls a Faerie, so Illusion Spinners has flash (can_play true); it is cast and, when it resolves, enters the battlefield.

variants.label: no-faerie
variants.delta: A controls Grizzly Bears instead of Faerie Miscreant.
variants.expected: Illegal: the condition is not met, so Illusion Spinners cannot be cast in B's end step (can_play false); it stays in A's hand.

scenarios.title: The alternative characteristics of an adventurer determine which half may be cast from the top of the library

setup.notes: Garruk's Horde: you may cast creature spells from the top of your library. Giant Killer (creature) has the Adventure Chop Down (instant, {2}{W}: destroy target creature with power 4 or greater). Giant Killer is the top card of A's library.

decisions: With Giant Killer on top of A's library and the stack empty, the game evaluates whether A may cast Giant Killer ({W}) and whether A may cast its Adventure Chop Down ({2}{W}, targeting Craw Wurm) from the library; A casts neither, so both verdicts are taken from the same state.

variants.label: horde
variants.expected: Giant Killer can be cast from the top of the library (can_play true) because it is a creature card; Chop Down cannot, because considered as an instant it is not a creature spell (can_play false).

variants.label: melek
variants.delta: Melek, Izzet Paragon is on A's battlefield instead of Garruk's Horde.
variants.expected: Chop Down can be cast from the top of the library (can_play true, Craw Wurm is a legal target); Giant Killer cannot, because it is not an instant or sorcery card (can_play false).

variants.label: neither
variants.delta: A controls neither Garruk's Horde nor Melek.
variants.expected: Neither Giant Killer nor Chop Down can be cast from the top of the library (can_play false for both).

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge may not model the adventure half's characteristics for MayPlay of a library card; check it is reachable.

scenarios.title: A player who is no longer allowed to cast the spell after proposal has the cast reverted

setup.notes: Void Winnower: your opponents can't cast spells with even mana values.

decisions: B starts casting Rolling Thunder and announces X = 2 (mana value 4), assigning its damage to A, tapping four Mountains.

variants.label: even-x
variants.expected: Illegal: the chosen X makes the spell's mana value even, so Void Winnower prohibits it; the cast is reverted: Rolling Thunder is in B's hand, the Mountains are untapped, the stack is empty and A's life is 20.

variants.label: odd-x
variants.delta: B announces X = 1 (mana value 3) instead of X = 2.
variants.expected: Legal: Rolling Thunder is cast with three Mountains tapped and, when it resolves, A's life is 19.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge's cast flow may never let B announce an X that makes the spell illegal.

scenarios.title: A prohibition that begins after the spell is cast does not undo the cast
decisions: A casts Shock targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Mountain; A passes priority.
B casts Silence in response, tapping Plains; B passes priority, then A passes priority; Silence resolves.
Both players pass priority again.

variants.label: silence-after-cast
variants.expected: Silence ('your opponents can't cast spells this turn') resolves after Shock was cast, so the cast stands: Shock stays on the stack, resolves, and Grizzly Bears (2 damage) moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: silence-first
variants.delta: B casts Silence before A casts Shock: A passes priority with an empty stack, B casts Silence and it resolves, then A has priority again and tries to cast Shock.
variants.expected: Illegal: A is prohibited from casting spells this turn, so Shock cannot be cast (can_play false) and stays in A's hand; Grizzly Bears is not damaged.

scenarios.title: A spell begun with flash because of a condition can finish being cast after the condition stops holding

setup.notes: Isamaru, Hound of Konda is a legendary creature attacking B. Scarring Memories ({3}{B}, sorcery): you may cast it as though it had flash if you control an attacking legendary creature. Phyrexian Altar: sacrifice a creature: add one mana of any color.

decisions: A, with priority in the declare attackers step, begins to cast Scarring Memories targeting B.
A pays {3}{B} by tapping three Swamps and activating Phyrexian Altar, sacrificing Isamaru, Hound of Konda.
Both players pass priority; Scarring Memories resolves.

variants.label: condition-lost
variants.expected: The condition held when the cast began (can_play true); sacrificing Isamaru while paying ends it, but the cast is completed: Isamaru is in A's graveyard, Scarring Memories is on the stack and, when it resolves, B sacrifices Grizzly Bears, discards Mountain, and loses 3 life (B's life is 17).

variants.label: never-held
variants.delta: The attacking creature is Grizzly Bears instead of Isamaru, Hound of Konda (not legendary).
variants.expected: The condition never holds: Scarring Memories cannot be cast in the declare attackers step (can_play false); it stays in A's hand and nothing is sacrificed.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge may or may not offer the mana ability's sacrifice as a payment source for a spell whose flash condition it removes; check it.

scenarios.title: Casting a spell that alters costs does not affect a spell already on the stack

setup.notes: Sphere of Resistance: spells cost {1} more to cast.

decisions: A casts Shock targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping one Mountain for {R}, and holds priority.
A casts Sphere of Resistance above Shock, tapping two Mountains.
Both players pass priority; Sphere of Resistance resolves and enters the battlefield.
Both players pass priority; Shock resolves.

variants.label: shock-first
variants.expected: Shock, cast for {R}, stays on the stack after Sphere of Resistance enters the battlefield with no further cost demanded; Shock resolves and Grizzly Bears is dealt 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: sphere-first
variants.delta: A casts Sphere of Resistance first and lets it resolve, then tries to cast Shock with the one Mountain left.
variants.expected: Shock's total cost is {1}{R} and A has one untapped Mountain: can_play false, Shock stays in A's hand and Grizzly Bears is undamaged; Sphere of Resistance is on A's battlefield.
